analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיֹּאמֶר. The words that follow, תַּדְשֵׁא הָאָרֶץ (‘Let the earth sprout’), give the command God spoke.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים, the third-person masculine singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר identifies God as the single speaker who commands the earth to sprout vegetation.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: In God's command תַּדְשֵׁא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׁא, הָאָרֶץ is the subject and the cognate noun דֶּשֶׁא names what the earth is to cause to sprout. The verse specifies seed-bearing plants and fruit trees.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil jussive, third person feminine singular, agreeing with הָאָרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: In תַּדְשֵׁא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׁא, הָאָרֶץ is the subject of the feminine singular verb תַּדְשֵׁא, ‘let it sprout.’ The article refers back to the dry land named in verse 10, which God now commands to produce vegetation.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + singular absolute common noun, with feminine singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: In תַּדְשֵׁא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׁא, “let the earth sprout vegetation,” דֶּשֶׁא is the cognate object of תַּדְשֵׁא. It names the green growth the earth is to produce.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The masculine singular participle מַזְרִיעַ agrees with עֵשֶׂב. The phrase עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע describes herbage that produces seed, alongside trees that bear fruit.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע, the plant yields seed. The parallel phrase עֵץ פְּרִי עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי describes a fruit tree bearing fruit.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil active participle, masculine singular absolute, modifying עֵשֶׂב.

analysis.evidence: In עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע, “vegetation producing seed,” זֶרַע is the direct object of מַזְרִיעַ and identifies what the vegetation produces.
עֵץ is in construct with פְּרִי, forming עֵץ פְּרִי ‘fruit tree’. The following עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי ‘bearing fruit’ describes the living tree.
The marked פְּרִי completes the construct phrase עֵץ פְּרִי, “fruit tree.” It identifies the tree by what it bears, as the following עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי, “bearing fruit,” confirms.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עֵץ פְּרִי עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי, the participle עֹשֶׂה agrees with עֵץ ‘tree’ and takes the second פְּרִי ‘fruit’ as its direct object. The phrase describes what the tree produces.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, modifying עֵץ.

analysis.evidence: The marked פְּרִי is the direct object of עֹשֶׂה in עֵץ פְּרִי עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי, “a fruit tree bearing fruit.” It names what the tree produces.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עֵץ פְּרִי עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי לְמִינוֹ, the phrase לְמִינוֹ describes how the fruit tree bears fruit. The suffix refers to the tree, and לְ marks conformity to its kind.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix וֹ.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the relative clause זַרְעוֹ בוֹ, “its seed is in it.” The possessive suffix on זַרְעוֹ gives the English rendering “whose seed is in it.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר זַרְעוֹ בוֹ, “whose seed is in it,” the verse describes a fruit-bearing tree with seed in its fruit. The same noun occurs earlier in מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע, “yielding seed.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: In עַל הָאָרֶץ, “on the earth,” עַל introduces the place where the vegetation is to grow.
In עַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל means “on” and identifies the ground as the surface on which the vegetation grows.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a common noun of common gender, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: כֵן (“so”) refers back to God’s command that the earth sprout vegetation. The closing words וַיְהִי כֵן mean “and it happened so,” affirming that the command was fulfilled.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי כֵן (“and it was so”), כֵן refers back to God’s command that the earth produce vegetation and affirms that it happened as commanded.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb without prefix or suffix.
